legend: Ariel is on a vacation where he must visit n%%ZSMJ0%% locations famous for their cereal, numbered 1…n%%ZSMJ1%%.
He will visit all the locations in some order, where the i%%ZSMJ2%%th location he visits is ai%%ZSMJ3%%.
Therefore, his order of visiting locations forms a permutation of length n%%ZSMJ4%%. Note that a permutation of length n%%ZSMJ5%% is a sequence containing every number from 1…n%%ZSMJ6%% exactly once.
Ariel thinks an amazing permutation is one where there are no indices (i,j,k)%%ZSMJ7%% where (1≤i<j<k≤n%%ZSMJ8%%) such that j−i=k−j%%ZSMJ9%% and aj−ai=ak−aj%%ZSMJ10%%.
Find a permutation of 1…n%%ZSMJ11%% that satisfies this (the i%%ZSMJ12%%th number is the i%%ZSMJ13%%th location Ariel visits).
output: A single line containing a space separated permutation of 1…n%%ZSMJ16%% such that Ariel has an amazing vacation.
Any output satisfying the above constraints will be accepted.
note: If we take the first sample case output, no three indices validate the above condition.
Another example would be (i,j,k)%%ZSMJ20%% = (1,2,3)%%ZSMJ21%%. Although, j−i=k−j%%ZSMJ22%% since 2−1=3−2%%ZSMJ23%%, aj−ai≠ak−aj%%ZSMJ24%% since 4−2≠2−1%%ZSMJ25%%.
